Will Signal rum out of money?
https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/824506840

Short version: solid no --- Signal’s burn is around $40-50 M/yr but its Foundation is sitting on >$1B in crypto and was last valued near $2.8B. They’d have to keep blowing cash for another ten-plus years just to empty the war-chest, and they're actively monetizing anyway.

Longer version:

- 2022 IRS filing (latest public Form 990) shows Signal Technology Foundation had net assets $1.03 **billion**, funded mainly by Acton’s giant $1.05 B crypto gift and cover-donations from Intel cofounder Andy Bryant and early PayPal guys.  
- Total spending in that filing was ~$48 M (fair chunk was market-rate staff salaries and double-digit AWS / CDN bills). Even though head-count has grown, the trend is nowhere close to outrunning that capital base.  
- Revenue lines: donor continuity + Acton’s on-going gifts + 2024’s beta Stripe-in-chat payment split add a trickle of fee income. They’re also experimenting with optional paid features without touching E2EE.  
- With crystal-ball 5% annual portfolio appreciation against the current burn, they’re break-even on Ops forever without raising another nickel. Even if crypto implodes, 200-year runway becomes 20-year runway; plenty of time to spin up a commercial tier à la WhatsApp Business API.

Bottom line: unless Acton pulls the money back or Telegram-style legal attacks create nine-figure new liabilities, Signal 2024 isn’t anywhere near insolvent — they’re effectively a VC-backed non-profit mint printing its own runway.
